QSVT realizes a bounded polynomial transformation through repeated matrix-access circuits and projector phases

. It applies to more than the special eigenvalues of the

The implementation supplies an original reciprocal polynomial, bounded deterministic phase fitting, explicit Hermitian Pauli PREPARE/SELECT/unprepare, a gate-built complex input and complete measured trials. Small circuits have independent numerical reference checks. The polynomial error is analytic; numerical access-angle construction and physical synthesis have separate limits. General non-Hermitian loading, an asymptotically optimal reciprocal compiler and Lean formalization remain planned.

A polynomial or stored-phase certificate does not certify floating PREPARE angles or an actual Clifford+T synthesis sequence. QDK’s mean-fit synthesis scalar is a cost model, rather than an operator-norm certificate for the postselected observable. Clean initialization/reset timing and faults, classical coefficient preprocessing, compilation, reference solve and readout/postprocessing timing are excluded from physical runtime and disclosed in the ledger. Dependency depth alone is not a hardware schedule.

Lowering preserves coherent action on arbitrary prepared data by disabling the assumption that all input qubits are initially zero. The pinned QASM exporter may omit the recorded overall compiled global phase. Downloads are consequently scoped to complete measured trials; they must not be used as phase-preserving controlled inverse oracles without retaining that phase.

The physical queries keep the pinned model and budgets and are bounded to eight wires, 25,000 primitive operations and 60 seconds per case. Factory costs, distances and capped serial runtime appear in every report. The CSV’s space-time proxy is peak footprint times serial duration, measured in qubit-seconds; it is not an integral of changing qubit occupancy.

Tests and independent reviews cover complex inputs, Y terms, different degrees, analytic phase derivatives, measured basis changes, gap-promise violations, coherent lowering and bounded workload guards. Dense amplitude/unitary loading is rejected by the preparation API.

offers a distinct positive-spectrum construction and actual known-input amplitude amplification. This QSVT method uses repeated access to the original Pauli matrix instead of classically expanding the reciprocal into new Pauli coefficients. General non-Hermitian block embeddings, better condition-dependent polynomials and certified physical synthesis are further variants. No Lean theorem or integrated formal proof currently covers this entire circuit.
